- Overestimate prices when sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.8) in recent days, especially after spikes; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is strongly bearish (≤0.2) or shows recent reversal; add 3–5% to forecast to avoid underreaction.
- Lagged forecasts tend to overreact to recent sentiment shifts; adjust by smoothing 3–5 day moving average of true values before forecasting.
- Overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days) — cap forecast at 10–15% above peak for 2–3 days.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 2–4% per day until convergence.
- Sentiment reversal (e.g., 0.8 → 0.2) triggers downward bias correction — reduce forecast by 3–5% for next 3 days.
- High sentiment + low recent price volatility → forecast should be conservative; reduce forecast by 2–4% to avoid overconfidence.
